title: Lecture 5: Sampling and Aliasing
summary: This lecture covers the principles of sampling continuous-time signals into computers, the definition of the Nyquist rate, the consequences of aliasing, and how anti-aliasing filters prevent it.

concepts.name: Sampling Rate
concepts.explanation: Signals are measured every T seconds, and the sampling rate f_s is defined as 1 over T.

concepts.name: Nyquist Rate
concepts.explanation: Two times the maximum frequency (2 * f_max) of a signal. Sampling faster than this allows a signal to be rebuilt perfectly from its samples.

concepts.name: Aliasing
concepts.explanation: When you sample too slowly, a higher frequency folds into a lower frequency alias. Once aliasing happens, it cannot be undone and the original information is lost.

concepts.name: Anti-Aliasing Filter
concepts.explanation: A low-pass filter placed before the sampler to remove everything above half of the sampling rate, which is why CD audio uses 44.1 kHz.

examPoints.point: Sample faster than twice the highest frequency.
examPoints.cue: Please remember this sentence exactly, because this will be on the mid-term.

examPoints.point: Compute the alias frequency when given a tone and sampling rate.
examPoints.cue: On the exam, I often give you a tone and the sampling rate, and you must compute the alias frequency. Practice that calculation.

quiz.question: What is the sampling rate fs defined as?
quiz.explanation: The lecturer states that the sampling rate fs is one over T.

quiz.question: What is two times Fmax called?
quiz.explanation: Two times f_max is called the Nyquist rate.

quiz.question: If you sample a 7 kHz tone at 10 kHz, what is the resulting alias frequency?
quiz.explanation: The half of the sampling rate is 5 kHz, so 7 kHz is above the limit. 10 minus 7 equals 3, giving a 3 kHz tone.

quiz.question: Why does CD audio use a 44.1 kHz sampling rate?
choices: Because human hearing stops around 20 kHz, leaving room for an anti-aliasing filter
Because computers can only store 44.1 thousand samples per second
Because 44.1 kHz is exactly twice the Nyquist rate of every instrument
Because it eliminates all need for a low-pass filter
quiz.explanation: Human hearing stops around 20 kHz, and 44.1 gives a little room for the filter.

quiz.question: What removes everything above half of the sampling rate before the sampler?
quiz.explanation: A low-pass filter (anti-aliasing filter) removes everything above half of the sampling rate.
